name: Mirandese

ancestors.notes: Old Portuguese (Aviz-period) adstrate: as Portuguese consolidated as the state language, the Leonese-speaking communities of Miranda, Rionor, and Guadramil faced intensifying pressure. Portuguese orthographic conventions (lh, nh, ã) penetrated the writing tradition.

notes: Mirandese (mirandés), spoken in the Miranda do Douro municipality, northeastern Portugal. Classified as Asturleonese. Recognised as a regional/minority language in Portugal since 1999. Retains archaic Asturleonese features: diphthongisation of Latin short /e/ and /o/ (written ⟨iê/ie⟩, ⟨uô/uo⟩), palatal lateral /ʎ/ preserved (written ⟨lh⟩ in all positions; a written initial ⟨l⟩ is plain [l]). Heavy Portuguese adstrate via official education and administration. Mirandese preserves the medieval four-way+ sibilant contrast that Portuguese lost, the hallmark of the language: (1) voiceless apico-alveolar /s̺/ ⟨s, ss⟩ and its voiced counterpart /z̺/ ⟨-s-⟩ between vowels and before a voiced consonant; (2) voiceless (pre)dorso-dental /s/ ⟨c (before e/i), ç⟩ and voiced /z/ ⟨z⟩; (3) postalveolar /ʃ/ ⟨x⟩ and /ʒ/ ⟨j, g (before e/i)⟩; (4) the affricate /tʃ/ ⟨ch⟩ (still an affricate, unlike modern European Portuguese). NOTATION CONVENTION (matches the TigreGotico/mirandese_g2p expert gold): the apical/dorsal CONTRAST is written by marking only the apical series with the ̺ diacritic (⟨s⟩ = /s̺/, /z̺/) and leaving the dorso-dental series unmarked (⟨c, ç, z⟩ = plain /s/, /z/); this is IPA-standard, keeps the phonemic contrast explicit, and avoids the over-narrow laminal ̻ diacritic the gold does not use. ⟨ç⟩ is a fricative, not an affricate, and occurs word-finally (rapaç, lhuç) where Portuguese writes -z. ⟨j⟩ is /ʒ/ (western Iberian, never the Asturian palatal ʝ) — ⟨y⟩ is the glide /j/. INITIAL L. A written initial ⟨l⟩ is [l] (lindo → [ˈlĩdu], litro → [ˈlitɾu]). Leite de Vasconcellos (1900, vol. I, §13, p. 188) gives "lĩ-ndo" with [l] and describes l as "Como em português na palavra lapa". The Latin initial L that became [ʎ] is written ⟨lh⟩ (§111, p. 259: "O L inicial latino mudou-se normalmente no mirandês central ou normal em lh"), so ⟨lh⟩ = /ʎ/ and ⟨nh⟩ = /ɲ/. LETTERS V AND Ê. ⟨v⟩ maps like ⟨b⟩ (§14, p. 193: "Na pronúncia normal mirandesa não existe differença entre b e v"): a stop at the start of a word and after a nasal, a spirant between vowels. ⟨ê⟩ is [e] (Convenção letter table E, PDF p. 9: seno, abiêspra); ⟨yê⟩ is [j] + [e]. The trigraphs ⟨anh, enh, inh, onh, unh⟩ are given explicitly (oral vowel + /ɲ/, e.g. danho → [ˈdaɲu]) so the greedy nasal-vowel digraph does not swallow the /ɲ/ of a following ⟨nh⟩. Nasal digraphs ⟨an, en, in, on, un⟩ realise Portuguese-adstrate nasal vowels /ɐ̃ ẽ ĩ õ ũ/ before a consonant or at word boundary (brando → [ˈbɾɐ̃du]); before a vowel they are oral vowel + /n/. ALLOPHONY (post-lexical, allophone_rules): coda /n/ assimilates in place to a following labial ([m]) or velar ([ŋ]). Ibero-Romance intervocalic voiced-stop spirantisation (⟨b d g⟩ → [β ð ɣ]) is a REAL native process — voiced stops lenite to [β ð ɣ] everywhere except after a pause or a nasal (Mateus & d'Andrade 2000:11; Ferreira & Raposo 1999; mwl Wikipedia phonology, "voiced stops /b d ɡ/ MAY be lenited as fricatives [β ð ɣ]"). It is applied PER PHONEME on the basis of the expert-human TigreGotico/mirandese_g2p gold measured at true oral-intervocalic positions (post-nasal excluded): /b/ is spirant-dominant (β:9/b:5), so MWL_SPIRANT_B rewrites intervocalic /b/→[β] (a net win on the human gold, PER 0.1901→0.1851). /ɡ/ is already spirantised to [ɣ] intervocalically at the positional_graphemes layer (⟨g⟩ intervocalic → [ɣ]), so no allophone rule is needed — adding one only misfires after a diphthong glide (eigual → gold stop [ɐjˈɡwal]). /d/, however, remains STOP-dominant intervocalically in the gold (d:13/ð:7) — the documented Asturleonese conservatism/occlusion of /d/, and the reason the Wikipedia wording is hedged ("may be") — so /d/ keeps its positional default [d] and /d/→[ð] is DELIBERATELY NOT applied as a rewrite (a blanket /d/ rule regresses this expert gold); [ð] stays declared in the `allophones` inventory for the lattice / downstream mwl_phonemizer where lexical conditioning is available. Word-onset and post-nasal /b d ɡ/ keep the stop. Pre-consonantal nasal digraphs ⟨an en in on un⟩ (and ⟨am…⟩) before ANY stop — voiceless or voiced ⟨mb nd ng nt…⟩ — nasalise the preceding vowel and the nasal is absorbed, with the following stop retained (brando→[ˈbɾɐ̃du], quando→[ˈkwɐ̃du], bufanda→[buˈfɐ̃dɐ], abandono→[abɐ̃ˈdonu], lhéngua→[ˈʎẽɡwɐ], sendo→[ˈs̺ẽdu], mirandés→[miɾɐ̃ˈdes̺]). This is the inherited Ibero-Romance nasal-vowel + AST_NASAL_ABSORB behaviour and matches the native-speaker gold (TigreGotico/mirandese_g2p) on every nasal+stop word; the earlier oral-digraph treatment (⟨mb nd ng⟩ kept as [mb nd ŋɡ] with an oral vowel) was contradicted by the gold and has been removed. The stressed open-mid realisations [ɛ ɔ] and the mid vowels [e o] give the broad mid nasals [ẽ õ] (MWL_NASAL_E_OPEN, AST_NASAL_e, AST_NASAL_o). Leite de Vasconcellos (1900, vol. I, §6, p. 180) gives nasal e as "Tão aberto como em berra" and nasal o as "Tão aberto como em obra"; the nasal table (§24, p. 201) gives "com e entre é e ê" and "com o entre ó e ô". His e and o are the Spanish ones (§22, p. 198). HUMAN-GOLD CALIBRATION (TigreGotico/mirandese_g2p, 219 words) vs Vasconcelos, Estudos de Philologia Mirandesa vol.1: (4) the preserved Leonese rising diphthongs are CLOSE — ⟨ie/iê⟩→[je], ⟨uo/uô⟩→[wo] — because Mirandese has a single intermediate mid /e o/ quality, "menos abertos que os nossos", and the ⟨ie⟩ nucleus is described as lying between [i] and [e] (Vasconcelos v1 §§2,4,10, pp.178-183); open [jɛ/wɔ] and stressed open [ɛ/ɔ] (fuorte→[ˈfwɔɾtɨ], era→[ˈɛɾɐ]) are non-contrastive allophonic variants of the same mid phoneme, not a separate target, so the spec does not force them. (5) ⟨ei⟩→[ej] is kept as the normative central value; Vasconcelos v1 §11 p.184 records general oscillation ei~ai (eigual~aigual, beilar~bailar), so the gold s [ɐj]/[aj] realisations (purmeiro→[puɾˈmɐjɾu]) are attested free variants, not errors. (6) ⟨s, ss⟩ and intervocalic ⟨-s-⟩ stay apico-alveolar [s̺]/[z̺] (Vasconcelos v1 §12 p.191, "análogo ao s castelhano", word-initial and ⟨ss⟩; intervocalic voiced counterpart), distinct from dorsal ⟨c/ç/z⟩ — the medieval sibilant contrast; the gold s plain [s]/[z] is notational under-marking, so the apical diacritic is retained. UNSTRESSED VOWEL QUALITY. The published description of central Mirandese gives the values the spec uses. Leite de Vasconcelos, Estudos de Philologia Mirandesa I (1900), describes the speech of Duas-Igrejas, which is the central variety this spec targets. His letter table (§24, p. 200) reads unstressed ⟨o⟩ as the Portuguese unstressed o, i.e. [u]; unstressed ⟨u⟩ as "quasi u port. em tu, rua"; and unstressed ⟨e⟩ as the Portuguese "e surdo", example "de", i.e. [ɨ]. The vowel-by-vowel description agrees: /u/ is "talvez mais fechado que em português, e parecido com o ou francês", closer than Portuguese rather than centralised, and it occurs stressed and unstressed alike (§2). The centralised [ʉ] and half-open [e̞] that appear in part of the TigreGotico/mirandese_g2p gold are one contributor's narrower notation rather than a described norm: under the same 'central' dialect tag the gold writes 65 [u] against 36 [ʉ] with no environment separating them (ˈbʉɫtiʉ and ɐˈdultu are both closed syllables), and word-final ⟨e⟩ splits 20 [ɨ] against 3 [e̞]. The spec keeps the broad [u] and [ɨ]. CODA /l/ is velarised [ɫ] (caldo → [ˈkaɫdu], sol → [ˈs̺oɫ]). Leite de Vasconcellos (1900, vol. I, §13, p. 188) lists a separate lateral that "Só existe em fim de syllaba (geralmente medial)" and "quando por si só constitue uma syllaba, como no artigo l antes de consoante", with "Este som existe em português em caldo, sol". §3 (p. 179) has the preceding vowel velarise with it, and §113 states that every word-final -l inherited from Latin -L is "gutturalizado". He writes the sound ⟨ł⟩ "só em notação phonetica" and plain ⟨l⟩ "no uso corrente", which is a choice of spelling and not a second sound. The mirandese_g2p gold writes coda [l] 14 times against [ɫ] 6; the spec follows LdV. The velarisation of the preceding vowel is not modelled. SIBILANT VOICING. The apical ⟨s⟩ is voiced to [z̺] before a voiced consonant, inside a word and across words (asno, mesmo, ls nius), and final ⟨ç⟩ is [z] before a voiced consonant in the next word (lhuç del cielo → [ˈʎuz ˈdel ...]; MWL_S_VOICING, MWL_FINAL_S_VOICING, MWL_FINAL_C_VOICING): Leite de Vasconcellos (1900, vol. I, §13, p. 190): "final de palavra antes de consoante sonora" and "em fim de palavra só póde ouvir-se quando a palavra seguinte começa por consoante sonora". Before a voiceless consonant, a vowel or a pause the sibilant stays voiceless. The article l before a consonant is [ɫ] (MWL_ARTICLE_L_VELAR).

sources.author: Mateus, M.H.M. & d'Andrade, E.
sources.title: The Phonology of Portuguese
sources.notes: p. 11: the voiced stops /b d ɡ/ are lenited to the fricatives/approximants [β ð ɣ] in all positions EXCEPT after a pause or a nasal, where they surface as stops [b d ɡ]. Grounds the intervocalic spirantisation rule (MWL_SPIRANT_B) and the post-nasal/onset stop exception; the same process is described for Mirandese by Ferreira & Raposo 1999 and the mwl Wikipedia phonology ("voiced stops /b d ɡ/ may be lenited as fricatives [β ð ɣ]").

sources.author: Vasconcelos, J. Leite de
sources.title: Estudos de Philologia Mirandesa
sources.notes: Foundational description of Mirandese phonology, including the six-sibilant system. Based on the speech of Duas-Igrejas (central Mirandese). §2 (pp. 173-179) describes each vowel; §13 (pp. 187 ff.) each consonant, including the coda-only velarised lateral; §24 (p. 200) tabulates the phonetic value of every letter by syllable type, and is the locator for unstressed ⟨o⟩ = Portuguese [u], unstressed ⟨u⟩ = [u], unstressed ⟨e⟩ = Portuguese "e surdo" [ɨ]. §24 (p. 201) tabulates the nasal vowels, including the "e surdo" nasal ẽ̥ [ɨ̃]. §§75-77 (pp. 237-239) give unstressed initial en- → ã-, medial -en- → ẽ̥ [ɨ̃], and final -em → the intermediate ḙ̃ [ə̃] (central, defined p. 178, nasal p. 180) or ẽ̥ [ɨ̃] (Sendinês). §113 (p. 265) covers word-final -l from Latin -L.

sources.author: Ferreira, M.B. & Raposo, D. (coords.)
sources.title: Convenção Ortográfica da Língua Mirandesa
sources.publisher: Câmara Municipal de Miranda do Douro / Centro de Linguística da Universidade de Lisboa
sources.notes: Official orthography. § L: word-initial l before vowel = /ʎ/ in traditional lexicon (bare l occurs only in loanwords/proper nouns/article). § Nasalidade: an/en/in/on/un are nasal-vowel digraphs at word boundaries; they do NOT nasalise sequences before onset consonants. § Sibilantes: six-way contrast s̺/z̺/s̻/z̻/ʃ/ʒ. § Ditongos: iê/ie = /je/ (stressed /jɛ/); uô/uo = /wo/ (stressed /wɔ/). § Acento: paroxytone default; oxytone for -r/-l/-z/-ç/-in/-un/-on/-is/-us/-ns/-ão endings.

sources.author: Ferreira, M.B. & Raposo, D. (coords.)
sources.title: Primeiro Aditamento à Convenção Ortográfica da Língua Mirandesa
sources.publisher: Câmara Municipal de Miranda do Douro / Centro de Linguística da Universidade de Lisboa
sources.notes: February 2000 addendum. Key provision: Sendinese speakers may optionally write word-initial l- (not lh-) to represent /l/ rather than /ʎ/ (e.g., luna/lhuna). Sendinese monophthongisation of iê→i and uô→u also codified. Source: secondary (studosmirandeses.blogs.sapo.pt, cursodemirandes.wordpress.com); standalone PDF not located.

sources.author: Ferreira, J.P., Chesi, C., Cho, H., Baldewijns, D., Braga, D. & Dias, M.
sources.title: On Mirandese Language Resources for Text-To-Speech
sources.publisher: Proceedings of SLTU-2014, St. Petersburg, pp. 87-92
sources.notes: Mirandese TTS phone set (43 phones). §2 notes "the rare nasal schwa"; §3.4 lists exn, a "voiced central high sonorant nasal vowel" [ɨ̃]. It gives no word list for that phone.

stress.notes: Convenção Ortográfica da Língua Mirandesa (1999) accentuation, Portuguese-based: paroxytone default; written accent (acute or tilde) overrides. Oxytone-attracting endings reflect Mirandese orthography: consonant-final r/l/z/ç (rapaç, Pertual, falar) and the final nasals written with -n in the Asturleonese manner — -in (camin, Sendin), -un, and the systematically oxytone -on class from Latin -ōnem (naçon, coraçon, Associaçon). Unmarked -an/-en verb endings stay paroxytone as in Portuguese -am/-em. cliticless_words are the monosyllabic function words (definite article l/la/ls/las and its prep+article contractions, the prepositions and coordinating conjunctions, and the enclitic object pronouns) that lean prosodically on their host and carry no word stress (Convenção §L article paradigm; the same proclitic/enclitic inventory #527 marks for Portuguese, given in Mirandese orthography).

allophone_rules.notes: Nasal place assimilation (Mateus & d'Andrade 2000 §3; general Ibero-Romance): a coda /n/ agrees in place with a following labial stop/nasal, surfacing as [m].
Nasal place assimilation (Mateus & d'Andrade 2000 §3): a coda /n/ agrees in place with a following velar stop, surfacing as [ŋ].

Intervocalic spirantisation, /b/ → [β] between vowels (rabudo → [rɐˈβudu], haber → [ɐˈβeɾ], nuobo → [ˈnwoβu]). This is the general Ibero-Romance lenition of voiced stops: in northern/central EP and Mirandese, /b d ɡ/ are realised as the fricatives/approximants [β ð ɣ] everywhere EXCEPT after a pause or a nasal (Mateus & d'Andrade 2000:11), which is why this rule is conditioned on a preceding vowel (the MWL_NASAL_* environments and word onset keep the stop). The Mirandese-specific process is attested by Ferreira & Raposo 1999 and the mwl Wikipedia phonology ("voiced stops /b d ɡ/ may be lenited as fricatives [β ð ɣ]"). Applied per-phoneme on the evidence of the expert-human TigreGotico/mirandese_g2p gold, measured at true oral-intervocalic positions (post-nasal excluded): /b/ is spirant-dominant (β:9 vs b:5), so this rule is a net win on the human gold (11 words corrected vs 6 lexically-conservative loan stops such as 'brabo', 'alternatibo' left over-spirantised — the residual lexical variability the downstream mwl_phonemizer can condition on). /ɡ/ is NOT given an allophone rule: intervocalic ⟨g⟩ is already spirantised to [ɣ] at the positional_graphemes layer, and an additional /ɡ/→[ɣ] rewrite misfires after the glide of a falling diphthong (eigual → gold [ɐjˈɡwal], stop retained). /d/ is NOT spirantised: intervocalic /d/ is stop-dominant in the gold (d:13 vs ð:7), the documented Asturleonese conservatism of /d/, so its positional default correctly stays [d] and [ð] remains only a lattice candidate.

Nasalisation of the unstressed/reduced central [ɐ] before a tautosyllabic coda nasal. The inherited AST_NASAL_a keys on the phoneme /a/, which is the stressed realisation; an unstressed ⟨an⟩ (the proclitic preposition 'an', or an unstressed -an word-ending) first reduces to [ɐ], so the base rule no longer matches and the coda /n/ was absorbed without nasalising (an → *[ɐ]). Unstressed -an/-en still nasalise in Mirandese (Convenção §Nasalidade), so [ɐ] → [ɐ̃]: an Miranda → [ɐ̃ miˈɾandɐ].

Unstressed ⟨e⟩ [ɨ] before a tautosyllabic coda nasal inside the word stays a central vowel and nasalises to [ɨ̃]. Leite de Vasconcellos (1900, vol. I, §76, p. 238): "A port. -en- (-em-) atono no interior de palavras corresponde em mir. -ẽ̥- (-e̥n-, -e̥m-)", with entender → antẽ̥dér, lembrar → lhẽ̥mbrar, ventura → bẽ̥ntura, and "O phenomeno normal porém é ẽ̥". The nasal list of §6 (p. 180) gives the same vowel as "e̥ — Ex.: stẽ̥nder". His ring below marks the "e surdo" [ɨ]; the nasal-vowel table (§24, p. 201) defines ẽ̥ as "i. é, e surdo (= e̥) nasal". Ferreira et al. (2014, §2, §3.4) list the same vowel in the Mirandese TTS phone set as "voiced central high sonorant nasal vowel" ("the rare nasal schwa"). The Convenção Ortográfica (1999) agrees: its letter table (PDF p. 9; the PDF prints no page numbers) gives ⟨e⟩ = [ɨ̃] in "bendima, centeno", and "Representação da nasalidade" (PDF p. 19) says "o en de bendima lê-se geralmente com um e muito fechado, quase mudo [ɨ]". Recorded disagreement: the mirandese_g2p gold writes [ẽ] in oucidental (ows̻idẽˈtal) but [ɨ̃] in antender and antentar. The rule requires a grapheme after the nasal, so it leaves a word-final -en to MWL_NASAL_E_REDUCED_FINAL. The p. 201 table also allows a stressed ẽ̥ but gives no word for it, so stressed [ɨ̃] is not modelled.

Unstressed word-final ⟨-en⟩ [ɨ] nasalises to the mid central vowel [ə̃] in central Mirandese. Leite de Vasconcellos (1900, vol. I, §77, p. 239): "A -em atono no fim de palavras corresponde em mirandês normal -ḙ̃ e em sendinês -ẽ̥", with amen → amḙ̃, amassem → amassḙ̃, têem → tenḙ̃, devem → debḙ̃. His e with a caret below is defined on p. 178: "Som que participa de ḁ e de e̥; posso por isso chamá-lo indeciso ou intermédio … Muito semelhante ao e allemão final em eine, Tage … Alguns phoneticistas representam estes últimos sons por ə". The nasal list of §6 (p. 180) gives it as "ḙ — Ex.: corrḙ̃", with note 1: "Só existe em fim de palavras (nos verbos). É ás vezes difficil distinguir nestes casos -ḙ̃ de -ẽ̥, -ḁ̃ (e ainda -ẽ̌?) atonos. O normal é porém -ḙ̃." Limit: the spec cannot tell a verb from another word, so the rule applies to every unstressed word-final -en. The variants -ẽ̥ [ɨ̃] and -ḁ̃ [ɐ̃] that p. 180 n. 1 records are not modelled. The Convenção (1999) gives no value for final unstressed -en. Recorded disagreement: the llm-generated mirandese_dict gold writes [ẽ] here (comen ˈkomẽ, sáben ˈs̺aβẽ, puoden ˈpwodẽ). mwl-x-sendim re-declares this id with [ɨ̃].

Nasalisation of the Leonese rising diphthong ⟨ie/ié⟩ [jɛ] before a tautosyllabic coda nasal, parallel to the inherited AST_NASAL_* rules that nasalise the simple vowels (a e i o u) in the same environment. The base rules key on single-segment nuclei, so a diphthong nucleus is not matched and its coda /n m/ was still absorbed (AST_NASAL_ABSORB) — yielding an oral vowel with a dropped nasal (bien → *[bjɛ]). Mirandese nasal mid vowels are close-mid, as in Portuguese (Mateus & d'Andrade 2000), so [jɛ] raises to [jẽ]: bien → [ˈbjẽ].

Nasalisation of the preserved Leonese rising diphthong ⟨uo/uô⟩ [wo]/[wɔ] before a tautosyllabic coda nasal (fuonte → [ˈfwõtɨ]), the back-vowel counterpart of MWL_NASAL_DIPHTHONG_JE. Both open [wɔ] and close [wo] raise to close-mid nasal [õ], as Portuguese nasal /o/ is always close-mid (Mateus & d'Andrade 2000).

Nasalisation of stressed open-mid [ɛ] (from marked ⟨é⟩) before a tautosyllabic coda nasal, to the broad mid nasal [ẽ]: lhéngua → [ˈʎẽɡwɐ]. Leite de Vasconcellos (1900, vol. I, §6, p. 180) gives nasal e as "Tão aberto como em berra" and nasal o as "Tão aberto como em obra"; the nasal table (§24, p. 201) gives "com e entre é e ê" and "com o entre ó e ô". His Mirandese e and o are "menos abertos que os nossos" (§4, p. 179), the Spanish e and o (§22, p. 198: "sons iguaes ao e, o hespanhoes"), so the nasal vowel is the mid vowel, written [ẽ õ]. Counterpart of MWL_NASAL_E_REDUCED for the stressed realisation.

Stressed e nasalises before a coda nasal, to the broad mid nasal [ẽ]. Leite de Vasconcellos (1900, vol. I, §6, p. 180): "drento, tẽ. Tão aberto como em berra." The nasal table (§24, p. 201) reads "com e entre é e ê". The value is the Mirandese mid e of §22, p. 198 ("sons iguaes ao e, o hespanhoes"). Overrides the inherited rule only to carry this citation.

Stressed o nasalises before a coda nasal, to the broad mid nasal [õ]. Leite de Vasconcellos (1900, vol. I, §6, p. 180): "pongo. Tão aberto como em obra." The nasal table (§24, p. 201) reads "com o entre ó e ô". The value is the Mirandese mid o of §22, p. 198 ("sons iguaes ao e, o hespanhoes"). Overrides the inherited rule only to carry this citation.

The apical s is voiced before a voiced consonant inside a word: asno → [ˈaz̺nu]. Leite de Vasconcellos (1900, vol. I, §13, p. 190), on the voiced apical: "Medial (e intervocalico), final de palavra antes de consoante sonora", with the examples rosa, asno, sabel and ls nius; and on the voiceless apical: "Final de syllaba (antes de consoante surda)". The Convenção Ortográfica (1999), § S, lists mesmo, smagar and cismar. Before a voiceless consonant s stays [s̺]: pasta. The glides [j w] are not treated as voiced consonants, because no source cited here says so.

Coda l is the velarised [ɫ]: caldo → [ˈkaɫdu], sol → [ˈs̺oɫ]. Leite de Vasconcellos (1900, vol. I, §13, p. 188): "Só existe em fim de syllaba (geralmente medial)" and "Este som existe em português em caldo, sol". He writes it ⟨ł⟩ "Só em notação phonetica" and ⟨l⟩ "no uso corrente". Onset l is [l] ("Como em português na palavra lapa"). The velarisation of the preceding vowel (§3, p. 179) is not modelled.

sandhi_rules.name: final apical s before a voiced consonant
sandhi_rules.notes: Word-final apical s is voiced before a voiced consonant in the next word: ls nius → [ɫz̺ ˈnjus̺]. Leite de Vasconcellos (1900, vol. I, §13, p. 190): "final de palavra antes de consoante sonora" (ls nius). Before a voiceless consonant, a vowel or a pause s stays [s̺]: "final de palavra (em pausa, ou antes de consoante surda)". The glides [j w] are not treated as voiced consonants.

sandhi_rules.name: final ç before a voiced consonant
sandhi_rules.notes: Word-final ⟨ç⟩ is [z] before a voiced consonant in the next word: lhuç del cielo → [ˈʎuz ˈdel ...]. Leite de Vasconcellos (1900, vol. I, §13, p. 190): "em fim de palavra só póde ouvir-se quando a palavra seguinte começa por consoante sonora: lhuç del cielo (pronúncia: lhuz del çielo)". The Convenção Ortográfica (1999), § Ç: "paç de la tiêrra" is read with [z]. Written final ⟨z⟩ is [z] already.

sandhi_rules.name: article l before a consonant
sandhi_rules.notes: The article l is the velarised [ɫ] before a consonant: l pai → [ɫ ˈpaj]. Leite de Vasconcellos (1900, vol. I, §13, p. 188): "quando por si só constitue uma syllaba, como no artigo l antes de consoante". Before a vowel the article l is not asserted to be velarised, and stays [l].
